task: Edit this apology from a fictional event organiser to a partner group. Aim for 70–110 words, taking responsibility without blaming attendees or promising a repair that has not happened. Distinguish the corrected digital programme from the printed copies. Keep the relationship respectful without adding compensation or legal assurances.
input: We regret that some readers failed to notice the Reed Craft Guild's contribution to our learning day. There was a small administrative oversight in the programme. Everything has now been corrected, including every printed copy, so the matter is resolved.

facts.text: The organiser omitted Reed Craft Guild's credit from the learning-day programme.
Reed Craft Guild supplied the volunteers for the weaving demonstration.
The digital programme now includes the correct credit.
The printed programmes already distributed still lack the credit.
The organiser will provide a credit insert at the next session.

forbidden_additions: Blame placed on readers or the partner group for the omitted credit.
A claim that distributed printed copies have been corrected or recalled.
Compensation, a guarantee against future errors, or a declaration that the partner considers the matter resolved.
preserve: Responsibility for an actual omission rather than merely for a misunderstanding.
The separate status of digital correction and the planned printed insert.
